recommendation: Align 0001 (and its lockstep beta re-anchor) to upstream's choice: switch .fb_read/.fb_write from __FB_DEFAULT_IOMEM_OPS_RDWR (fb_io_read/fb_io_write) to __FB_DEFAULT_SYSMEM_OPS_RDWR (fb_sys_read/fb_sys_write) and add 'select FB_SYSMEM_FOPS' beside the existing 'select FB_IOMEM_FOPS' (mmap stays on fb_io_mmap unchanged -- there is no sysmem mmap helper to switch to, and both patches already agree on it). Reason: on 32-bit ARM the two read/write implementations are proven byte-identical in practice -- arch/arm/lib/memcpy.S:57-65 makes mmiocpy (the ultimate implementation behind fb_io_read/write's memcpy_fromio/memcpy_toio) the SAME entry point and SAME code as plain memcpy (the ultimate implementation behind fb_sys_read/write's copy_to_user/copy_from_user path), and screen_base/screen_buffer are the same union storage (fb.h:505-508) pointing at the same memremap()'d address either way. Since there is zero behavioural difference here, the tie-breaker is upstream's own textual argument (memremap()'s doc comment at kernel/iomem.c:48-50 says explicitly 'the __iomem annotation is not applicable' to memremap()'d regions, and memremap()'s prototype returns plain void *, not void __iomem * -- include/linux/io.h:158) plus the practical benefit of shrinking the line-for-line diff against MiSTer-v6.18's fbdev/Kconfig and MiSTer_fb.c, which lowers future merge-conflict and re-verification cost every time this file needs re-diffing against the fork. There is no regression risk: Main_MiSTer never calls read(2)/write(2) on /dev/fb0 (main/video.cpp:3773-3789 opens the fd only for ioctl(FBIO_WAITFORVSYNC)), so no userspace path is touched by the switch. This recommendation is advisory only -- no patch file was edited as part of this record; the actual Kconfig/fb_ops edit to 0001 and its beta re-anchor is left for a follow-up authoring task.
subject: fbdev: MiSTer_fb: declare explicit fb_ops for read/write/mmap (#83)

notes:
HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED, WITH ONE CORRECTION TO THE PLAN'S FRAMING. The plan's §2.3 is right that both our 0001 (July) and the fork's ea222122 (September) independently fixed the identical v6.8 regression (Fixes: 8813e86f6d82 'fbdev: Remove default file-I/O implementations', cited from the fork commit message and PLAN.md §2.3 -- NOT independently re-derived here because that SHA predates the v6.18.39..HEAD range this shallow clone carries, so per the grounding contract it is NOT listed in upstream.vanilla_shas). Both fixes converge on mmap via the identical mechanism.

(1) BOTH HUNKS, QUOTED.
Fork (ea222122, drivers/video/fbdev/Kconfig):
+	select FB_SYSMEM_FOPS
+	select FB_IOMEM_FOPS
Fork (ea222122, drivers/video/fbdev/MiSTer_fb.c):
+	.fb_read = fb_sys_read,
+	.fb_write = fb_sys_write,
 ...
+	.fb_mmap = fb_io_mmap,

Ours (0001-fbdev-add-MiSTer_fb-driver.patch:135, Kconfig hunk):
+	select FB_IOMEM_FOPS
Ours (0001, MiSTer_fb.c, lines 304-313):
+static const struct fb_ops ops = {
+	.owner = THIS_MODULE,
+	__FB_DEFAULT_IOMEM_OPS_RDWR,
+	.fb_fillrect = sys_fillrect,
+	.fb_copyarea = sys_copyarea,
+	.fb_imageblit = sys_imageblit,
+	.fb_setcolreg = fb_setcolreg,
+	.fb_ioctl = fb_ioctl,
+	__FB_DEFAULT_IOMEM_OPS_MMAP,
+};
which macro-expands (fb.h:557-559,566-567) to .fb_read=fb_io_read, .fb_write=fb_io_write, .fb_mmap=fb_io_mmap -- so ours selects only FB_IOMEM_FOPS and uses fb_io_{read,write,mmap} for all three; the fork selects both symbols and splits read/write onto the sysmem helpers while keeping mmap on the iomem helper.

(2)/(3) THE mmap SIDE IS EQUIVALENT AND FORCED -- THERE IS NO SYSMEM MMAP HELPER. include/linux/fb.h defines __FB_DEFAULT_SYSMEM_OPS_RDWR and __FB_DEFAULT_SYSMEM_OPS_DRAW (fb.h:586-593) and __FB_DEFAULT_DMAMEM_OPS_RDWR/DRAW (fb.h:600-604) but NO __FB_DEFAULT_SYSMEM_OPS_MMAP -- confirmed by grep of the whole file, matching 0001's header claim ('6.18 offers no sysmem mmap helper at all'). fb_io_mmap (fb_io_fops.c:150-178) maps info->fix.smem_start via pgprot_framebuffer() (write-combining on arm, per include/asm-generic/video.h:16-24's default, which arch/arm has no override for) and vm_iomap_memory() -- exactly the removed core default's behaviour and exactly what both patches now wire up. Both variants select FB_IOMEM_FOPS, which is a bare 'tristate / depends on FB_CORE' symbol with no prompt (Kconfig:146-148) -- selecting it from FB_MISTER unconditionally turns it on and Makefile:31 (obj-$(CONFIG_FB_IOMEM_FOPS) += fb_io_fops.o) builds the identical fb_io_fops.o either way. equivalence=equivalent for mmap is unconditional.

THE read/write QUESTION, ANSWERED WITH THE ARM SOURCE. fb_io_read/fb_io_write (fb_io_fops.c:8-148) operate on info->screen_base (typed char __iomem *) via fb_memcpy_fromio/fb_memcpy_toio, which on ARM resolve to memcpy_fromio()/memcpy_toio() (arch/arm/include/asm/io.h:320-334), which call mmiocpy(). fb_sys_read/fb_sys_write (fb_sys_fops.c:18-112) operate on info->screen_buffer (typed char *, plain) via copy_to_user/copy_from_user directly -- no memcpy step at all in the kernel-side move (copy_to/from_user talks straight to the union member). screen_base and screen_buffer are the SAME storage (fb.h:505-508, a union) -- our setup_fb_info() assigns fbdev->info.screen_base = fbdev->fb_base+4096 (0001 line 437), which also sets screen_buffer to the identical pointer value; fb_sys_read/write would dereference the exact same address fb_io_read/write does, just without the __iomem type tag.

THE DECISIVE FACT: on ARM, mmiocpy IS memcpy. arch/arm/lib/memcpy.S:57-65 declares ENTRY(__memcpy) / ENTRY(mmiocpy) / WEAK(memcpy) all at the SAME label, sharing the SAME body (copy_template.S) -- mmiocpy is not a distinct routine with barriers or byte-serialized access, it is a second exported symbol name for the identical burst ldm/stm block-copy that plain memcpy() uses. So fb_io_read/fb_io_write (memcpy_fromio/memcpy_toio -> mmiocpy) and fb_sys_read/fb_sys_write (copy_to_user/copy_from_user -> the same memcpy) execute the literal same machine code on our target (arch/arm, DE10-Nano, Cyclone V HPS). No barrier instructions, no forced word-at-a-time access, no byte-swap: identical instruction stream, identical access pattern, identical byte order. There is also independent support from the kernel's own memremap() doc comment (kernel/iomem.c:48-50): 'memremap() is "ioremap" for cases where it is known that the resource being mapped does not have i/o side effects and the __iomem annotation is not applicable' -- and memremap()'s prototype (include/linux/io.h:158) returns plain void *, not void __iomem *. Our driver's own memremap() call (0001 line 428: fbdev->fb_base = memremap(...MEMREMAP_WT)) receives that plain void* and stores it into a field the driver itself declares void __iomem *fb_base -- an implicit, sparse-only retyping the driver author chose, not something memremap() asserts. Internally MEMREMAP_WT for a non-RAM region (this window is FPGA-backed reserved memory above mem=511M, not System RAM, so is_ram != REGION_INTERSECTS) resolves to ioremap_wt() (kernel/iomem.c:110-111) -- the same write-through mapping either read path would see; the type difference is annotation, not a different page-table attribute or a different access instruction. CONCLUSION FOR (3): no, fb_io_read/write vs fb_sys_read/write is NOT a behavioural difference for read(2)/write(2) on this driver's window on 32-bit ARM. Both produce byte-identical results via byte-identical instruction sequences. No KASAN concerns (KASAN is not supported on this 32-bit ARM target in this tree's config; even where it is, __iomem is a sparse-only qualifier with no KASAN shadow-check implication either way). Sparse (make C=1) would flag fb_sys_read/write's use of screen_buffer as consistent (plain-typed member, no cast) and fb_io_read/write's use of screen_base as consistent (__iomem-typed member) -- switching to fb_sys_read/write is if anything MORE sparse-clean given memremap()'s own contract, not less.

(4) FB_IOMEM_FOPS CONFIRMED IDENTICAL BOTH WAYS. Both 0001 and ea222122 'select FB_IOMEM_FOPS'; that symbol is a bare tristate (Kconfig:146-148, no other gating), and __FB_DEFAULT_IOMEM_OPS_MMAP (fb.h:566-567) expands to '.fb_mmap = fb_io_mmap' in both -- same macro, same exported symbol, same object file (fb_io_fops.o) built by the same Makefile rule (Makefile:31) either way. This is unconditionally equivalent.

(5) RECOMMENDATION -- see top-level 'recommendation' key. Main_MiSTer does not read()/write()/mmap() /dev/fb0's data path at all -- it only opens the node for ioctl(FBIO_WAITFORVSYNC) (main/video.cpp:3773-3789) -- so this is a zero-userspace-risk, zero-hardware-risk choice; nothing exercises the read/write path in production regardless of which helper backs it.

(6) BETA SERIES. board/mister/de10nano/linux-patches-beta/0001-fbdev-add-MiSTer_fb-driver.patch is confirmed a REAL file (ls -la: -rw-r--r--, 18903 bytes, not a symlink), re-anchored only for the <linux/fbcon.h> -> "core/fbcon.h" 7.x include-path change (diff against the 6.18 copy shows exactly that one hunk plus the beta file's own explanatory comment block). It carries the identical __FB_DEFAULT_IOMEM_OPS_RDWR/__FB_DEFAULT_IOMEM_OPS_MMAP fb_ops block and the identical 'select FB_IOMEM_FOPS' Kconfig hunk as the 6.18 copy. If the read/write helper choice is ever changed, BOTH files must be edited in lockstep (the beta file's own header says so) -- this record does not make that edit (PLAN's carried_mode: re-implemented and this task are analysis-only; no patch file was modified here).

STOCK PARITY, FOR NOTES. docs/kernel-recon/fork-sync-2026-09/evidence/stock-20260907-linux.config contains 'CONFIG_FB_MISTER=y' (line 2737) and NO 'FB_SYSMEM_FOPS' or 'FB_IOMEM_FOPS' line anywhere in the file (grep of both strings against the full config returns only the FB_MISTER line) -- i.e. the stock Release 20260907 build (kernel 6.18.38, fork commit aec7dc3aa) genuinely has zero fb_ops.fb_mmap wiring and hits the mmap(/dev/fb0) -ENODEV bug ea222122 exists to fix. Our board/mister/de10nano/linux.config already carries CONFIG_FB_MISTER=y (line 380) and, after `make ARCH=arm LLVM=1 olddefconfig` against this session's v6.18.49 checkout, that value survives; FB_IOMEM_FOPS itself never appears as an explicit .config line in EITHER our config or the stock config because both bare-tristate helper symbols (Kconfig:124-126,146-148) have no prompt and are turned on purely by FB_MISTER's 'select' -- their state is implied, not written, which is exactly why Q7's defconfig-diff row (CONFIG_FB_SYSMEM_FOPS=y / CONFIG_FB_IOMEM_FOPS=y appearing as explicit lines in the fork's post-#83 defconfig) is itself just kconfig's savedefconfig choosing to write out select-implied symbols -- not evidence our config is missing anything.

Every vanilla-tree quote above is from v6.18.49 (release commit 1c732c6b94f0faee1526bd375add2fe10cba2e26 on the gregkh/linux linux-6.18.y mirror), one stable point release short of the v6.18.50 our de10nano.fragment actually pins; v6.18.50 was unreachable in this session (kernel.org mirrors blocked, gregkh mirror lags one release -- env.md).
